[[265.12]] 80. DAMARIS LADY MASHAM AN LEIBNIZ

[[265.13]] Oates, 8. (19.) August 1704. [76.90.]

[[266.1]] S^#'r Oates 8 August 1704.

[[266.2]] Whatever Am Kopf der Seite von Leibniz' Hand: resp. allowances are to be made for the Language of Civilitie to Ladys, differing but

[[266.3]] little from what would look like Flatterie to one of your own Sex; Yet I find a Pleasure in being

[[266.4]] Prais'd by You, which I Justifie to my self from a Beleefe that when you Honour me with such

[[266.5]] Expressions of your good opinion, You make me the Best return in Your power for that well

[[266.6]] Grounded Esteeme I have for You, by a Desire which That has created in You of finding me

[[266.7]] Worthy of Yours. Nor shall I ever reckon it a small matter if I have Desert enough to engage

[[266.8]] Those of a distinguish'd Merit to wish that I had more. Thus, if I do flatter my self, I am by a

[[266.9]] Vanitie but very little moderated, or rather Refin'd beyond that of Others, pleas'd with the

[[266.10]] favorable things you say of me, without that Cruel allay attending this Satisfaction which a

[[266.11]] Consciousness of not resembl'ing the Picture you have made for me must otherwise give me.

[[266.12]] Whether I have rightly represented Your Systeme You Best can tell: and what you say on

[[266.13]] that Subject I am proud of; Whilst the Inferences you would draw from thence to my advantage

[[266.14]] can give me onely a Due acknowledgment for your wishing me so much fitter for your

[[266.15]] Correspondence than I am. But however justly I may have express'd your Sense so far as I

[[266.16]] indeavour'd to represent it, your Answers to some of my Enquiries makes me question whether

[[266.17]] I fully apprehend All that is included in your Hypothesis. For I do not yet sufficiently see upon

[[266.18]] what you ground Organism's being Essential to Matter: or indeed very well understand

[[266.19]] your Meaning in these Words That Organisme is not absolutely Essential to Matter but to

[[266.20]] Matter arrangée par une Sagesse Souveraine. What you would Build upon this, Forms a

[[266.21]] very Transcendant Conception of the Divine Artifice; and such as I think could onely occur to

[[266.22]] the thoughts of one possess'd with the highest admiration of the Wisdome of his Maker: But if

[[266.23]] you infer the Truth of this Notion onely from its being the most Agreable one that you can

[[266.24]] Frame to that Attribute of God, this, Singly, seemes to me not to be Concludeing: Since we can,

[[266.25]] in my opinion, onely infer from thence that whatsoever God dos must be according to infinite

[[266.26]] Wisdome: but are not able with our short and narrow Views to determine what the operations of

[[266.27]] an Infinitely Wise Being must be.

[[266.28]] The Principle of Action call'd by you Force Primitive is you say a Substance: of

[[266.29]] the which, I still perceive not the positive Idea Perception being but the Action of this

[[266.30]] Substance: what you add concerning its Perceptions, in these words, suivant l'Analogie

[[266.31]] qu'elle doit avoir avec notre ame, makes me again beleeve that I do not fully understand

[[266.32]] your scheme: since I thought before that the Soul and this Force Primitive, or Principle of

[[267.1]] Action, had been the same thing. You say renfermer les Ames dans les Dimensions

[[267.2]] c'est Vouloir imaginer les ames comme des corps. in regard of Extension this is True;

[[267.3]] and Extension is to me, inseparable from the notion of All Substance. I am yet sensible That

[[267.4]] we ought not to reject Truths because they are not Imaginable by us (where there is Ground to

[[267.5]] admit them). But Truth being but the attributeing certain affections conceiv'd to belong to the

[[267.6]] subject in question. I can by no meanes attribute any thing to a subject whereof I have no

[[267.7]] Conception at all; as I am Conscious to my self I have not of Unextended Substance. What you

[[267.8]] instance in therefore of Lines Incommensurable seemes not to me to answer the Case; for I

[[267.9]] herein do conceive the Proposition, and have Cleare Ideas of Lines Incommensurable, thō I

[[267.10]] do not see the reason of theire Incommensurabilitie: but of an unextended substance I have

[[267.11]] not any Conception, from whence I can affirm, or Deny, any thing concerning it.

[[267.12]] Why you think that theire is no Created Substance Complete without Extension:

[[267.13]] or that the Soul (which you suppose a distinct substance) would without the Body be a

[[267.14]] Substance Incompleat without Extension, I understand not: but my owne Beleefe that there is

[[267.15]] no Substance whatever Unextended is (as I have alreadie said), grounded upon this that I have

[[267.16]] no Conception of such a thing. I cannot yet but Conceive two very different Substances to be in

[[267.17]] the Universe, thō Extension alike agrees to them Both. For I clearly conceive an Extension

[[267.18]] without Soliditie, and a solid Extension: to some system of which last if it should be

[[267.19]] affirm'd that God did annex Thought, I see no absurditie in this from there being Nothing in

[[267.20]] Extension and Impenetrabilitie or Soliditie, from whence thought can naturally, or by

[[267.21]] a train of Causes be deriv'd; the which I Beleeve to be Demonstrable it cannot be. But That was

[[267.22]] never suppos'd by me; and my Question in the case would be This: Whether God could not as

[[267.23]] conceivably by us as create an unextended Substance, and then unite it to an Extended

[[267.24]] substance (wherin, by the way, there is methinks on your Side two difficulties for one) Whether

[[267.25]] God, I say, could not as conceivably by us as his Doing This would be, Add (if he so Pleas'd)

[[267.26]] the Power of Thinking to that Substance which has Soliditie. Soliditie and Thought

[[267.27]] being both of them but attributes of some unknown Substance and I see not why it may not be

[[267.28]] one and the same which is the common Support of Both These; there appearing to me no

[[267.29]] contradiction in a so existence of Thought and Soliditie in the same Substance. Neither can I

[[267.30]] apprehend it to be more Inexplicable That God should give Thought to a Substance which I

[[267.31]] know not, but whereof I know some of its attributes, than to another, suppos'd, Substance of

[[267.32]] whose very Being I have no Conception at all. and that any Substance whatsoever should have

[[267.33]] Thought belonging to it, or resulting from it, otherwise than as God has Will'd it shall have so,

[[267.34]] I cannot Apprehend.

[[267.35]] That God dos in Frameing and Ordening of all his Works always make use of the most

[[267.36]] simple meanes I doubt not, this appearing to me most sutable to his Wisdome, but whether, or

[[267.37]] no, these simple meanes or methods are always such as Surpass not a Created intelligence, I do

[[268.1]] not know: but am very apt to Beleeve That Gods Ways are Past our finding out, in this

[[268.2]] sense.

[[268.3]] I have no sooner scribled to you these Thoughts of mine, than I feare Wearying You by my

[[268.4]] Dulness. I shall therefore Wave takeing notice of any thing more that has occur'd to me in

[[268.5]] Considering the several parts of your letter; or makeing any such farther inquiries as perhaps

[[268.6]] were there resolv'd, I might be able in some measure to cleare to my self. I will however now

[[268.7]] mention to you one difficultie (as I conceive) in your Hypothesis, which I think not that I could

[[268.8]] ever extricate it from without your assistance, and it is to me a very material one. Viz how to

[[268.9]] reconcile your Systeme to Libertie or Free Agencie: for thō in regard of any Compulsion

[[268.10]] from other Causes, we are according thereto Free, yet I see not how we can be so in respect of

[[268.11]] the first Mover. This I omitted takeing notice of in my last not onely because I thought it too

[[268.12]] remote an inquiry for one who wanted to be inlighten'd concerning the very foundation you

[[268.13]] Built upon: but also because I must acknowledge that I cannot make out Libertie either With,

[[268.14]] or Without any Hypothesis Whatsoever. Thō as being persuaded that I feel myself a Free

[[268.15]] Agent, and that Freedome to Act is necessarie to our being Accountable for our Actions, I

[[268.16]] not onelie conclude we are indu'd therewith, but am very tenacious hereof: whence I should be

[[268.17]] sorry to find from any new Hypothesis new difficulties in maintaining of this. I think not much

[[268.18]] that I need seek to Justifie to you the part which I own my Inclination has in this Opinion; since

[[268.19]] what you have said in Print persuades me that you have the same Beleef with the same Bias. I

[[268.20]] might else perhaps, alledge (in my excuse at least), that as I am a True English Woman, I cannot

[[268.21]] but naturally have a Passion for Libertie in All senses wherein I consider it: and I would not

[[268.22]] have so Much as the Philosophy of Hanover Unfavourable to any Kind of it.

[[268.23]] What you write on the subject of M^#'r Locke's health, he is much oblig'd by: and I am no

[[268.24]] less so when You recommend to me the care of one of the Best Friends I have in the World as a

[[268.25]] matter in which you interess your self. If I could contribute to the Prolonging so Valuable a Life

[[268.26]] as his, I should think this one of the best uses I could ever make of my own. He is not onely still

[[268.27]] with me, but in all Probabilitie will never have health enough to permit him the thoughts of

[[268.28]] Leaving any more a place which he has made Agreable to Others by haveing for many years

[[268.29]] chosen to spend therein a great Part of his Time. Rational Conversation, with Mutual Good

[[268.30]] Will, has the greatest Charmes that I know in Life, and I have hitherto been very Happy in

[[268.31]] respect of that Enjoyment. To my Felicitie in which kind I think it a considerable addition to be

[[268.32]] Honour'd with Your Correspondence at such a Distance, and that I am allow'd to assure you of

[[268.33]] my being with great Esteeme

[[268.34]] S^#'r Your Most Humble Servant Da Masham.
